title: Documentation: Add CLAUDE.md and docs for AI coding assistants
body:
Closes #

<!-- If your PR is related to an issue, provide the number(s) above; if it resolves multiple issues, be sure to break them up (e.g. "closes #1000, closes #1001"). -->

<!--

Thank you for contributing to Storybook! Please submit all PRs to the `next` branch unless they are specific to the current release. Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

-->

## What I did

Consolidated repository instructions for coding agents.

This PR:

- adds `AGENTS.md` as the canonical instruction file
- changes `CLAUDE.md` to a thin `@AGENTS.md` reference
- adds `.agents/skills/` as the canonical home for agent skills
- keeps `.claude/skills/` as thin references to the matching `.agents` skills
- removes `.github/copilot-instructions.md` so the guidance is no longer duplicated

The goal is to keep one maintained instruction source while preserving the existing skill-based workflows.

comments.author: valentinpalkovic

comments.author: valentinpalkovic
comments.body: From my experience, AI often messes up with `yarn task` commands if they are not properly described. My personal opinion is that we list the 10 most common scenarios on how to do certain things (build a sandbox, run a sandbox, run Vitest, run an e2e test, ...)
comments.label_reasoning: The documentation lacks enough concrete examples/scenarios for common tasks, making it unclear for AI agents to correctly use the 'yarn task' commands.

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Sounds good to me.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests adding the 10 most common usage scenarios to the documentation to prevent AI mistakes.

comments.author: valentinpalkovic
comments.body:
Copilot often messes up with this by defining the file relative to root, instead of relative to `code`. We should clarify this step a bit more. Something like:

```suggestion
yarn --cwd code lint:js:cmd <file-relative-to-code-folder> --fix
```
comments.label_reasoning: The lint command documentation is ambiguous about the file path reference (root vs. code folder), leading to AI agents making mistakes. Needs clarification.

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Agreed

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests clarifying the lint command to specify the file path should be relative to the code folder, with a specific suggestion.
